keyframe_review.note: New keyframe at confidence 1: Cliopatria drops the league in 189, but as a client 'required... to minister to the power and empire of the Roman people' it existed until the Roman settlement of 146, when 'all leagues and other political entities were dissolved' (Achaean War page). The Aetolian War page (the Roman-Seleucid war article) and the Marcus Fulvius Nobilior page were opened: neither names a territorial clause ('completely broke the power of the Aetolian League', 'reduced to a Roman client state'), so the extent of the cantons' departure remains a reading.

ledger.note: 367 (earliest suggested founding): the league 'received Aeolis from the Thebans' in 367; 'its founding date is uncertain, with suggestions ranging from 367 BC to later'; infobox 'Established: 4th century BC'. Confidence 1 for the year; the koinon certainly existed by 338.

Which state held it before Philip is not on the pages opened (the Naupactus page has it pass to the Achaeans, then to Epaminondas, then back to the Locrians), hence the Macedonian counterpart; macedonian-empire records the mirror loss and its own gain from greek-city-states at confidence 1. June 197: Cynoscephalae ('In June 197 BC, Flamininus marched north from Elateia'). In 196 'the Aetolians wanted the return of Thessalian cities they had once held. Flamininus refused to back them': no Thessalian gain.

192: the Aetolians seize Demetrias. 'The Aetolians then moved troops to seize Sparta, Chalcis, and Demetrias' (Aetolian League page, 192, the war with Rome); only Demetrias fell to them. The page names no previous holder: Demetrias had been a Roman-freed city since 196 (antigonid-dynasty), so the counterpart is the catch-all greek-city-states.

region.text: Thessaly and Aetolia, the war with Rome

After Thermopylae (191) and Magnesia (190) the Romans turned on Aetolia (Ambracia besieged 189).

191: Philip V takes Demetrias. 'The spring of 191 BC saw the Macedonians enter the war against the Aetolian League' (Roman-Seleucid war page); Demetrias is among the places Rome let Philip keep (Philip V page, undated). Mirrors antigonid-dynasty's 191 gain from this league.

notes:
Cliopatria's 'Aetolian League' (-284..-189, 7.5-11.8 k km2) is extended at both ends: back to 367 (new keyframes 367-302 and 301-285, confidence 1 and 2) and forward as a Roman client (rule 4 tint) from 189 to 146 (new keyframe, confidence 1). The main correction is the forty-year freeze of 271-231: the league's growth to its peak (the Acarnanian share c. 250, the central Greek cantons in the 240s-230s, Ambracia c. 233) falls inside it, and Cliopatria never draws the cantons east of Parnassus except in 208. Those cantons' accession dates are not on the Aetolian League page (which lists them undated as the peak membership) and are entered as a single confidence-1 step in 245; a gap-filler should open 'Phocis', 'Locris', 'Malis' and 'Dolopia'. Disagreements: the client status 189 (text) or 188 (infobox); Ambracia to Pyrrhus 295 (Epirus infobox) or 294 (Ambracia and Arta pages). Not on the pages opened and left out: the Boeotian alliance of 245, the Elean and Messenian alliances, the Peace of Naupactus's year (inferred from the infobox), the 189 clauses on Amphilochia, Cephallenia, Oeniadae and Acarnania, the Thessalian Phthiotis-Malis accessions, and the Aetolian seats at Delphi after 189. 'Aetolia' and 'Acarnania' are not gazetteer regions: Cliopatria polygons, Central Greece minus Boeotia and Euboea, and radii stand in (reported under gazetteer_names_needed). The 'Aetolian_War' URL serves the Roman-Seleucid war article, which is what is cited.

Fix run of 2026-10-19 (after the adversarial review). Changed: (1) the 188-146 keyframe is now Aetolia proper plus Naupactus, as its text always said, and a 189 loss of the central Greek cantons backs it (confidence 1: the Roman-Seleucid war page, the Aetolian League page and the Marcus Fulvius Nobilior page, all opened, name no territorial clause; Nobilior 'completely broke the power of the Aetolian League'). (2) The corrections of 210-189 now subtract Achaia Phthiotis (lost 217) and, from 208, Epicnemidian and Opuntian Locris (lost 208), which no event regains. (3) Demetrias: a 192 gain from greek-city-states (Aetolian League page: 'The Aetolians then moved troops to seize Sparta, Chalcis, and Demetrias', only Demetrias fell) and a 191 loss to antigonid-dynasty, whose 191 event now names the Aetolians for Demetrias only. (4) The Social War contest with achaean-league is a ledger pair now (the war entry already named it as a belligerent). (5) The Naupactus note no longer says 'after Chaeronea' or that Philip took it from the Achaeans, which neither the Aetolian League nor the Naupactus page says. Kept: Ambracia 233 against kingdom-of-epirus's 231 (the Epirus page: 'the Aetolians seized Ambracia around 233 BC'); kingdom-of-epirus should move its loss to 233. Two Aetolian events now have their Macedonian mirrors in antigonid-dynasty (211, 210, 208, 219) and macedonian-empire (338).
